title: Inclusion of contracted fibre components in a common semistable model
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-kun-separably-closed], and let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for each $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Suppose the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(C,D)$ have smooth generic curve and etale generic marking. Let $f:(X,F)\to(C,D)$ be a stable $\eta$-modification and $g:(Y,G)\to(C,D)$ a semistable $\eta$-modification. Suppose $(W,E)$ is semistable and $a:(W,E)\to(X,F)$ and $b:(W,E)\to(Y,G)$ are $\eta$-modifications with $fa=gb$. For every $s\in S$ and every irreducible component $Z$ of $W_s$, if $b_s(Z)$ is a point then $a_s(Z)$ is a point. This asserts only an inclusion of the sets of contracted fibre components; it does not assume or conclude a morphism $Y\to X$. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and a component $Z\subset W_s$ with $b_s(Z)$ a singleton. By [lem-trf-sepclosed-valuation-geometric-components], $k=\kappa(s)$ is separably closed. An algebraic closure $\Omega/k$ is purely inseparable by [lem-pc-kbar-pure-insep]. Thus [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep] makes the projections $W_\Omega\to W_s$, $X_\Omega\to X_s$ and $Y_\Omega\to Y_s$ homeomorphisms. Let $\bar Z$ be the component corresponding to $Z$. The base-change diagrams commute and their vertical maps are bijective, so $b_\Omega(\bar Z)$ is a singleton. These same diagrams will descend the assertion for $a$. This argument concerns topological images and does not assume that $Z$ stays irreducible under a general field extension.

proof.text: Since $f$, $g$, $a$ and $b$ are isomorphisms on the generic pairs, the generic curves of $X$, $Y$ and $W$ are smooth and their generic markings are etale. The sources and targets of $a$ and $b$ are semistable multipointed $S$-curves: for $X$ this is included in stability of $f$, and for $Y$ in semistability of $g$. Apply [lem-trf-semistable-modification-fibre-contractions] separately to $a$ and $b$, retaining their given family $\eta$-modification hypotheses. It gives finite elementary exceptional-contraction sequences for both $a_\Omega$ and $b_\Omega$, with proper quotient maps, semistable intermediate pairs and compatible markings. This supplies the precise blowdown hypothesis; no claim of modification or a common dense open for the whole geometric-fibre maps is needed. By [lem-trf-semistable-marked-base-change], $f_\Omega$ has the geometric stability predicate as well as semistable source.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.3(i), printed p. 31; Lemma 4.4.2 and Appendix Lemma B.3. Online primary text read; archival PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Put $r=f_\Omega a_\Omega=g_\Omega b_\Omega:W_\Omega\to C_\Omega$. Every component contracted at a stage of the $a_\Omega$ sequence has singleton image under the remaining map to $X_\Omega$, hence under its composite with $f_\Omega$; thus that stage is $r$-exceptional. The same argument using $g_\Omega$ applies to the $b_\Omega$ sequence. The terminal $a_\Omega$ quotient has induced map $f_\Omega$ and has no exceptional component by Step 2. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-stable-blowdown-uniqueness] with $\pi=a_\Omega$ and $q=b_\Omega$: it gives $a_\Omega=u\circ b_\Omega$ for a morphism of geometric pointed curves. Therefore $a_\Omega(\bar Z)=u(b_\Omega(\bar Z))$ is a singleton. The cited result concerns explicit contraction sequences, so no connectedness of $W_\Omega$ and no unproved comparison of fibre genera is being assumed.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.3(i), printed p. 31; Lemma 4.4.2 and Appendix Lemma B.3. Online primary text read; archival PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Write $p_W:W_\Omega\to W_s$ and $p_X:X_\Omega\to X_s$. By Step 1, $p_W(\bar Z)=Z$ and $p_Xa_\Omega=a_sp_W$. Consequently $a_s(Z)=p_X(a_\Omega(\bar Z))$ is a singleton. Since $s$ and $Z$ were arbitrary, this proves the asserted inclusion of contracted fibre components.
